name: Question 7
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+2y(t)-6 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=x(t)-3y(t)+{y}^{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the corresponding linearized system at the equilibrium point ${x}^{∗}=[2,\text{ }1]^{T}?$

| ${u}^{′}=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,u,\,$ where $u=x-{x}^{∗}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2y-6 \\ x-3y+{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2y-6)=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2y-6)=2 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-3y+{y}^{2})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-3y+{y}^{2})=-3+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x & 2 \\ 1 & 2y-3\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2(2) & 2 \\ 1 & 2(1)-3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, near the equilibrium, the nonlinear system is approximated by

$$
{u}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]u,
$$

where the deviation vector is

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x-2 \\ y-1\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

The system can be rewritten in matrix form as x′=f(x) where x=[x(t)y(t)] and f(x)=[x2+2y−6x−3y+y2].

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of f(x).

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f2∂x∂f2∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(x2+2y−6)=2x,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(x2+2y−6)=2∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x−3y+y2)=1,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x−3y+y2)=−3+2y

Thus, we have

f′(x)=[2x212y−3].

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium x∗=[21] to get

f′(x∗)=[2(2)212(1)−3]=[421−1].

Finally, near the equilibrium, the nonlinear system is approximated by

u′=[421−1]u,

where the deviation vector is

u=x−x∗=[xy]−[21]=[x−2y−1].
